ara (Sales): Heads-up — VP-eng at AtlasMed asked for a precise reserved-GPU + autoscale plan before legal signs. They want preheat behavior, burst policy, and cost estimate. Can we sync quick?

sophia (Solutions Eng): Sure. Does AtlasMed have a traffic profile we can use? key dims: peak RPS, avg request token length, response token distribution, and concurrency targets (p95 latency).

ara (Sales): I have their spec: peak 1.8k requests/min (~30 r/s) but a lot of bursts up to 200 r/s for 90s. Avg prompt 120 tokens, avg response 220 tokens. Target p95 < 600ms for chat endpoint.

mike (Infra): Quick notebook math: for the model they're picking, one A100-equivalent GPU yields ~250 warm short-chat requests/sec at 2048 context if responses are ~200 tokens with streaming disabled. For their avg sizes, assume ~120 req/s/GPU. For bursts, use autoscale + burst credits. Suggested baseline: reserved_gpus=2 to cover steady state (~240 r/s headroom), autoscale up to 8 for bursts. Preheat policy to maintain KV cache for 10min when scaled up.

mike (Infra): Example policy snippet we can hand to legal/ops:

```yaml
reserved_gpus: 2
min_replicas: 1
max_replicas: 8
burst_policy:
  burst_credits: 900     # token-equivalent credits, ~15min of short bursts
  recharge_window_s: 600
preheat_seconds: 600    # KV warm window after scale-up
scaling_cooldown_s: 60
latency_slo_p95_ms: 600
```

sophia (Solutions Eng): Notes: 1) We recommend a canary for first 72h of traffic to validate latency/quality under reserved capacity. 2) If they require encrypted keys in HSM, preheat timing may be longer. 3) For deterministic billing, we can convert preheat into committed prewarm hours (see finance).

jake (Finance): Pricing questions: do we charge for preheat as part of reserved commit, or as metered prewarm? AtlasMed prefers a simple monthly committed GPU-hours line item. Proposal: include 200 prewarm hours/month into committed package (rolled into committed price), with a clear overage rate (e.g., 1.8x list for on-demand). I'll draft numbers once we lock reserved_gpus and expected utilization.

emily (Customer Success): Operational runbook item: schedule a dry-run where AtlasMed replays 2 x peak for 30min to validate autoscale behavior. We'll need access window and a point-of-contact for warmup. Also capture logs for token-level cost breakdown.

ara (Sales): Perfect. Action items: @sophia to confirm model throughput per-GPU for their chosen model variant; @mike to produce a short one-pager with the YAML + explanation for legal; @jake to sketch committed-hours pricing bands; @emily to coordinate the replay window with AtlasMed. I'll consolidate and send to their engineering lead.

oncall-bot: Created incident-playback channel #inc-playback-atlasmed (auto-created)

mike (Infra): One more caveat — AZ-affinity: recommend we spread reserved GPUs across 2 AZs for durability. If they want single-AZ cheaper config, call it out in the MSA as a risk. :warning:

sophia (Solutions Eng): I'll attach throughput test data and a short perf matrix (tokens/sec vs GPU type) in the doc we hand off.

ara (Sales): Thanks all — I'll ping AtlasMed this afternoon with the draft plan and ask for the replay window. :thumbsup:
